name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 21 points
Carson has raised $1M with $621K on hand; challenger shows no reported fundraising

model.rationale: The Indianapolis-based seat's 21-point Democratic lean, Carson's incumbency and roughly $1 million war chest against a Republican nominee with no reported fundraising, and prediction markets pricing a Carson win at 96-97 percent all point to a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or significant outside spending for McAuley would be the first sign of trouble, though nothing currently suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson, the Democratic incumbent in this Indianapolis-based district, seeks another term with the structural advantages of a seat that leans Democratic by about twenty-one points. He has raised roughly one million dollars and holds more than six hundred thousand on hand, while Republican nominee Patrick McAuley shows no reported fundraising. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot, which may trim the Democratic margin slightly without threatening the outcome.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign money. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price a Carson win at roughly ninety-six to ninety-seven percent, consistent with the district's lean. The seat sits firmly in the safe Democratic column, and the main open question is the size of the victory margin rather than who wins.
